findings.title: Sudoers rule is wider than its header claims and is root-equivalent
findings.description:
The header says "exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider", but the rule is wider in three ways.
- **Writable installer:** `MT_INSTALL` lets `manta` run, as root, a script under `/home/manta/source/repos/...`. The `manta` user can edit that file, so the rule gives full root.
- **Wildcards match spaces:** sudoers `*` also matches spaces and further arguments. `systemctl stop mt-* ` therefore accepts `systemctl stop mt-x sshd.service`. `mt-run *` and `--ref *` accept arbitrary arguments in the same way.
- **Secrets file:** `MT_READ` hands out the secrets file `/etc/manta-trading.env` as root.

The install comment also runs `visudo -c` only after the file is installed, so a syntax error would break sudo before it is caught. Validate first with `visudo -cf deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops`. Run the installer from a root-owned path, and either narrow the wildcards or drop the "nothing wider" claim.

findings.title: Removing the weekend tolerance can bring back the endless re-fetch
findings.description: When no session closes inside the chunk, the function keeps the `classify_outcome` verdict. The deleted block existed to turn PARTIAL into SUCCESS for a chunk that ends on a non-trading day. A legacy row that spans only a weekend or holiday, or a chunk whose sessions are missing from `trading_sessions` (unverified), now stays PARTIAL. It will be re-fetched forever with `attempt_count` climbing, which is the failure the old comment described. The tests do not cover a chunk with no judgeable session and bars from before the chunk. Decide the outcome for that case explicitly and test it.

findings.title: The cagg freshness check compares against the wrong timestamp
findings.description:
`last_successful_finish` is compared with the newest `created_at`. A refresh that started before the bars were written but finished after them reads as fresh, although the bars were not materialised. `last_successful_start` is the safer comparison, and the refresh policy's end offset could also exclude recent buckets. Two things I could not check:
- Whether `job.hypertable_name` equals the cagg name `minute_4hour_ohlcv`. For cagg policies it may be the `_materialized_hypertable_N` name. If so, the query returns no row, `last_refresh` is None, and `--verify` would answer WAIT indefinitely whenever bars exist.
- The test that checks `max(created_at)` mocks the cursor, so it would not catch either problem. An integration test against TimescaleDB would.

findings.title: The `[WAIT]` and `FAIL` verdicts are matched as scattered strings
findings.description: The repair script prints `[WAIT]`, and the cutover script matches `"[WAIT]"` in three places plus `"FAIL"` in two. The project rules say a value used in comparisons must be defined once, and that user-visible labels must not carry logic. Define the markers as constants shared by both scripts, or return a structured verdict instead of parsing printed text.

findings.title: A second pooled connection is opened per chunk while the first is held
findings.description: `fetch_session_bounds` runs on a new `pool.connection()` inside a function that already holds `conn`, and the advisory lock may also be held (the lock is acquired in this function in the code under review). With a small pool and several workers, this risks pool starvation. The query also runs for outcomes that `judge_chunk_by_sessions` immediately passes through, such as EMPTY and TRANSIENT_FAILURE. Reuse `conn`, or fetch the bounds only when the outcome is SUCCESS or PARTIAL and the response has bars.

findings.title: Import ordering will fail the required ruff `I` rule
findings.description:
Several import blocks are not sorted:
- `NOTES_DIR`, `fire_unit_until` and `start_log` are placed before `CutoverError` in the `cutover_common` import in `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py`.
- `cagg_freshness_for_session` precedes `CheckReport` in the `repair_921` imports in `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py` and `test/unit/test_repair_921.py`.
- The `minute_sessions` and `repair_921` imports in `daemon/minute.py` are inserted between the other `data.gaps` imports.

Run `ruff check --fix`.

findings.title: `bar_timestamp` duplicates the bar-parsing logic
findings.description: The docstring says it "mirrors `_bar_to_row`". The diff removes one duplicate parser (`_latest_bar_dt`) and adds another. Have `_bar_to_row` call `bar_timestamp`, so the two cannot drift apart.

findings.title: Part of the cutover narration is not written to the log file
findings.description: `start_log` is described as the cutover's record, but only `say` writes to it. The `print` calls for polling status and for the `mt-run` command line go to the terminal only. `start_log` also truncates an existing file and keeps its path in a module-level global, so a second call silently discards the first log.

findings.title: Test setup is copied between tests
findings.description: `test_last_bar_before_the_chunk_end_is_still_success` repeats about 50 lines of pool, lock and patch setup that `_run` already provides. Extend `_run` to take the gap and the session bounds. The other new tests, including the one that checks the chunk is judged per session, are otherwise behaviour-focused and good.
